Note::NlpAccessor::remove_code¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::remove_code() const

Delete Code-Shaped Spans Without Parsing A Language¶

remove_code() removes common prose-embedded code forms: inline backtick spans, fenced blocks, and indented code lines. It is appropriate when natural language surrounding code is the desired result. It is not a programming- language parser and does not inspect syntax inside the removed region.

Code form

Recognition rule

Removed extent

Inline

A pair of single backticks on one line

Both backticks and all enclosed bytes.

Backtick fence

A closed pair of triple-backtick fences

Opening fence, optional language label, body, and closing fence.

Tilde fence

A closed pair of triple-tilde fences

Opening fence, body, and closing fence.

Indented line

At least four leading ASCII spaces, or a leading tab

The complete line.

Fenced matching may cross line boundaries and selects the shortest closed span. Inline matching never crosses a newline. An unclosed backtick or fence is not removed: without a closing delimiter, the method preserves the original cell exactly. This conservative rule avoids discarding a document suffix after truncated markup. The method does not recognize language-specific comments, HTML elements, dollar-delimited mathematics, or bare expressions without one of the structural forms above.

After a real removal, surviving ASCII whitespace is collapsed and stripped, so blank lines left by a deleted block do not remain. With no removal, every byte is retained. Multiple code forms in one cell are handled in one call.

The output is a fresh, shape-preserving Text Note; code removal never changes rank or cell count. A code-only cell becomes an empty text cell. Empty Text Notes remain empty, undefined propagates, and Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject. Cheap byte and indentation prechecks bypass regular-expression work for cells that cannot contain a supported code form.

Example 1: Inline, Fenced, And Indented Code Together¶

const auto source = pluss::note::make({
    "Keep `inline()` here.\n```cpp\nint x;\n```\n"
    "    indented();\n\talso_indented();\nplain",
});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(source.nlp().remove_code()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Keep here. plain"]

Example 2: An Indented Block May Begin On The First Line¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"    hidden();\nvisible"})
        .nlp().remove_code()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["visible"]

Example 3: Tilde Fences Are Also Code Fences¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"~~~\nhidden();\n~~~\nvisible"})
        .nlp().remove_code()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["visible"]

Example 4: Unmatched Syntax Is A True No-Op¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"  an unmatched `\nremains  "})
        .nlp().remove_code()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["  an unmatched `\nremains  "]

Example 5: Process Cells Independently Without Flattening¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"Copyright 2026", "a (draft)",
                             "- item", "use `x` now"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.nlp().remove_code()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["Copyright 2026", "a (draft)"], 
  ["- item", "use now"]
]

Example 6: Empty, Undefined, And Invalid Dtypes¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::string>{}).nlp().remove_code())
          << '\n';
std::cout << "undefined defined=" << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().remove_code().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes(
      std::vector<std::string>{"`x`"},
      std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{1}).nlp().remove_code();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "Bytes: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
undefined defined=false
Bytes: rejected

Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject for the same reason.
